summary:
- Focus exclusively on immediate human bodily phenomena rather than external food manufacturing or general trivia.
- Address the viewer directly in the first 3 words using 'Your' or 'You' to create instant personal relevance.
- Keep script length strictly between 17 and 18 seconds to maximize average view percentage.
- Omit emojis from video titles, as text-only titles out-performed emoji titles by over 5x in views.
- State a surprising or counter-intuitive fact about the viewer's current state in the hook rather than asking a rhetorical question.
winning_hooks: Direct second-person body claims (e.g., 'Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.')
Short, confrontational state-of-being declarations (e.g., 'You are not sad when you chop an onion.')
avoid: Passive/informational openers about facts (e.g., 'Honey is famous for being...')
Rhetorical questions about everyday items (e.g., 'That sweet maple syrup on your pancakes?')
Adding decorative emojis to video titles
next_experiment: Test a body-centric hook ('Your stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve metal right now') against a general trivia hook ('Stomach acid is one of the strongest liquids on earth') using the exact same 17-second script body and clean title format.
